result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would erase the concept of "otherness"—the idea that difference implies separation or opposition. Not by enforcing uniformity, but by dismantling the fear and scarcity that make us hoard power, resources, or identity at the expense of others.

Imagine a world where no one is "less than" because of where they were born, how they worship, whom they love, or what they own. Where systems aren’t built on extraction, but on the understanding that harm to one is harm to all. Where curiosity replaces suspicion, and collaboration outshines competition.

It wouldn’t solve everything—human complexity would remain—but it might unclench the fists of history.
